role: Member B -- frozen single-arm grasp scene and physics parameters
frozen_source_rule: droid_cube_scene.xml is read-only. Never regenerate it -- build_droid_object_scene.py:ensure_scene() overwrites it from folding_scene_V25_4_TOWEL_SUPPORT_04.xml when the mtimes line up. Run this script with --verify to detect that.

object.note: rgba red is what the monocular perception mask keys on; friction[0]=1.0 is the sliding coefficient the grasp relies on.

camera.name: workspace_camera
camera.role: monocular workspace camera for cube localisation

intrinsics_640x480.note: square pixels assumed; validated by silhouette IoU 0.954 at the ground-truth pose

render_check.note: a camera aimed the wrong way renders black without raising anything, so the build renders one frame and refuses to write a config if it is essentially black

grasp.axis_policy: MUST BE PINNED. search_reachable_grasp() picks whichever of the six signed world axes has the lowest IK residual, and that winner flips between calls (measured: y- at 18.1 mm residual, then y+ at 9.8 mm after the target moved). Different signed axes are mirror images, so anything that corrects the grasp across calls must hold the axis fixed. This also explains run-to-run differences of the same plan (2 contacts in one run, 0 in another).
grasp.calibration_method: Close once, read the contact centroid in the object frame, shift the requested grasp centre by minus that, repeat. Converged in 5 passes from 37.0 mm off centre to 4.2 mm off centre.

contact_model.reason: The imported pad mesh yields one point on each opposing cube face. condim=4 models the torsional resistance of a finite pad contact patch; no weld is used.

grasp.known_limitation: The 5-pass recentring is a calibration procedure, not an execution path: 5 passes x ~8 s of sim far exceeds the task book's 15 s budget. For a fixed scene, calibrate once and bake the offset in; the episode itself is then a single pass.

validation_scope: MJCF compile of the frozen scene plus the wrapper camera, and the physics parameters read back out of the compiled model. The grasp numbers come from a closed-loop measurement in this scene. NOT verified here: perception accuracy on other object poses, the 15 s budget, or anything outside the right arm.
